query: How do I set up an SSH key on Linux?
answer:
Start by creating a key pair with `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "you@example.com"`. Ed25519 is the modern recommended key type. If a legacy system doesn't support it, use `ssh-keygen -t rsa -b 4096` instead [1][2]. Press Enter to accept the default location (`~/.ssh/id_ed25519`), and set a passphrase when asked. That creates a private key, `id_ed25519`, which you should never share, and a public key, `id_ed25519.pub`, which is the one you give to servers and services like GitHub [3]. Make sure only you can read the private key with `chmod 600 ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` [4].

To log in to a server with the key, run `ssh-copy-id user@host`. It asks for your password one last time and adds your public key to the server's `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`. If the server uses a non-standard port, add `-p 2222` (or whatever the port is) [3][2]. After that, `ssh user@host` should log you in with the key. To avoid typing your passphrase every time, load the key into the agent with `ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519`. For GitHub, paste the contents of the `.pub` file into your account's SSH keys settings, then test the connection with `ssh -T git@github.com` [3].
